```{r Write problems intro}
#| output: asis

# One of the report's texts in its language, or in English where po4a
# withheld the translation for falling below its completeness threshold,
# which it reports only by the file's absence.
localized_text_file <- function(name) {
  localized <- file.path(language, name)
  if (file.exists(localized))
    return(localized)
  logWarn("Text not available in this language, using English: ", name)
  file.path("en", name)
}

# A report with nothing to report says so and leaves out the introduction,
# the problem details, and the solutions, which all cross-reference sections
# that exist only when there are findings to explain; an administrator's
# appendix can still follow. Where the exception list exempted records, the
# sentence says that it did; with findings, the hint on requesting an
# exception comes first, and a note on warnings follows the introduction
# where a warning found one.
if (nrow(problems) == 0L) {
  cat(if (records_exempted) sR$no_problems_detected_exempted else sR$no_problems_detected, "\n")
} else {
  cat("", "::: {.callout-note}",
      paste("##", sR$exception_request_hint_title),
      "",
      exception_request_hint(sR, support_email_address),
      ":::", "", sep = "\n")
  cat(
    sep = "\n",
    knitr::knit_child(text = readr::read_file(localized_text_file("_problems_intro.Rmd")), quiet = TRUE),
    ""
  )
  if (any(problems$rule_id %in% warning_rule_ids))
    cat(sR$problems_warning_note, "", sep = "\n")
}
```

{{< include _problems.qmd >}}

```{r Write problem details}
#| output: asis

if (nrow(problems) > 0L) {

cat("::: {.content-visible unless-format=\"html\"}", "\\newpage", ":::", "", sep = "\n")

# Problem details intro
cat(
  sep = "\n",
  knitr::knit_child(text = readr::read_file(localized_text_file("_problem_details_intro.Rmd")), quiet = TRUE),
  ""
)

# Problem details
sortedDetails <- problem_detail_info |>
  dplyr::semi_join(
    problem_info |>
      dplyr::filter(id %in% report_problems) |>
      dplyr::select(usedDetails) |>
      tidyr::unnest_longer(usedDetails),
    dplyr::join_by(id == usedDetails)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(sortOrder) |>
  dplyr::mutate(filePath = paste0(language, "/_problem_detail_", sprintf("%04d", id), ".Rmd")) |>
  dplyr::select(filePath, usedSolutions) |>
  dplyr::distinct()

# po4a omits a localized problem-detail file whenever its translation falls
# below the completeness threshold, and the absence is reported by the file
# simply not being there — so resolving these by glob dropped the problem's
# explanation from the report with no error and no trace. Fall back to the
# English source, which is always present, so an untranslated detail degrades
# to English rather than to silence.
localized_details <- sortedDetails$filePath
english_details <- sub("^[^/]+/", "en/", localized_details)
untranslated <- !file.exists(localized_details)

if (any(untranslated))
  logWarn("Problem detail(s) not available in this language, using English: ",
          paste(basename(localized_details[untranslated]), collapse = ", "))

problem_detail_files <- ifelse(untranslated, english_details, localized_details)
absent <- !file.exists(problem_detail_files)

if (any(absent))
  logError("Problem detail(s) missing in every language: ",
           paste(basename(problem_detail_files[absent]), collapse = ", "))

problem_detail_files <- problem_detail_files[!absent]

# Every child is followed by a blank line of its own. A file that ends without
# a final newline would otherwise run straight into the next file's first line,
# and Pandoc reads a heading or a fence on the line after a paragraph as part
# of that paragraph — so a `:::` opening the next file became literal text.
for (problem_detail_file in problem_detail_files) {
  cat(sep = "\n", knitr::knit_child(quiet = TRUE, text = readr::read_file(problem_detail_file)), "")
}

cat("::: {.content-visible unless-format=\"html\"}", "\\newpage", ":::", "", sep = "\n")

# Solutions intro
cat(
  sep = "\n",
  knitr::knit_child(text = readr::read_file(localized_text_file("_solutions_intro.Rmd")), quiet = TRUE),
  ""
)

# Solutions: the ones the included details draw on, closed over the solutions
# those cite in turn, in the catalogue's order. A solution po4a withheld for
# want of translation falls back to English, as a detail does; resolving the
# paths by glob dropped it silently and left every reference to it dangling.
solution_ids <- close_solutions(unlist(sortedDetails$usedSolutions))
localized_solutions <- solution_info |>
  dplyr::filter(id %in% solution_ids) |>
  dplyr::arrange(sortOrder) |>
  dplyr::mutate(filePath = paste0(language, "/_solution_", sprintf("%04d", id), ".Rmd"), .keep = "none") |>
  dplyr::pull(filePath)
english_solutions <- sub("^[^/]+/", "en/", localized_solutions)
untranslated_solutions <- !file.exists(localized_solutions)

if (any(untranslated_solutions))
  logWarn("Solution(s) not available in this language, using English: ",
          paste(basename(localized_solutions[untranslated_solutions]), collapse = ", "))

solution_files <- ifelse(untranslated_solutions, english_solutions, localized_solutions)

for (solution_file in solution_files) {
  cat(sep = "\n", knitr::knit_child(quiet = TRUE, text = readr::read_file(solution_file)), "")
}

}
```
